newsitem.title: UK: Bildt says troops must stay in Bosnia till 1998.
newsitem.headline: Bildt says troops must stay in Bosnia till 1998.

text.p: International Bosnia peace coordinator Carl Bildt said on Thursday foreign contingents of troops would have to remain in Bosnia in 1997 and 1998 for the country to stand any chance of recovering from the recent war.

"The mission of this military presence would primarily be deterrent, to provide reassurance that there are no military options and no military threat, thus providing the conditions necessary for political reconciliation, re-integration and reconstruction," he said in a speech in London.

There are currently around 53,000 peacekeepers under a NATO-led command but their mandate expires on December 20 and no decision has been taken on the presence of foreign troops in Bosnia after that date.
NATO is pushing for a follow-on force with a U.S. presence to remain in Bosnia after December.

"Without an outside deterrent force in the country such efforts could easily become destabilising whereas they could be a long-term investment in military restructuring and stability if such a force is in place," Bildt said.
